title: POS Paper & Receipts for Cafés: What Every Owner Should Know
description: A practical guide to thermal receipt paper for cafés and coffee shops — sizes, BPA-free options, and how the right roll keeps your printers running.
body:
Behind every espresso shot and pasty is a printer quietly spitting out receipts. When it jams or runs dry mid-rush, the whole line stalls. Choosing the right thermal paper for your café keeps service moving, extends your printer's life, and saves you from reprinting faded receipts later.

Match the roll to your printer — not the other way around

Most café POS systems and register printers take standard 2¼-inch (58mm) or 3⅛-inch (80mm) thermal rolls. The width is non-negotiable: a roll that's even slightly off will misalign, jam, or print cut-off text.

  • 2¼" (58mm) — common for compact register printers and handheld order takers.
  • 3⅛" (80mm) — standard for full counter printers and kitchen order printers that need wider tickets.

Check the model label on your printer or the inside of the paper door — it usually lists the exact width and core size. If you're unsure, grab the existing roll and match its dimensions.

BPA-free matters when your team touches receipts all day

Baristas and cashiers handle dozens of receipts per shift. BPA-free thermal paper removes the concern of phenol-based coatings transferring through skin contact. It costs slightly more per roll, but for a café with high hand-contact it's a smart, low-effort upgrade — and a point you can quietly stand behind with your team.

Buy in bulk, store it right

Thermal paper is sensitive to heat and light. A box stored next to the oven or in a sunny window will yellow and fade before you use it. Keep rolls in their box, in a cool dry spot, and buy in volume you'll actually turn over — thermal paper does have a shelf life, so a two-month supply is usually the sweet spot for a busy café.

What to keep on hand

  • A spare case of your exact roll size so you never run out mid-shift.
  • A cleaning card or isopropyl wipe to keep the printhead clear of paper dust and residue.
  • A backup printer if your counter runs high volume — kitchen and front counter often need different widths.

Conclusion: small choices, smoother service

The right paper, the right size, and the right storage are three small decisions that keep your café's service fast and your receipts legible. Take five minutes to confirm your printer's specs, switch to BPA-free if you haven't, and set up a simple reorder cadence so you're never caught short.
